items: Drop `on Type` to group fields under one directive
Same tool, different job: grouping, not narrowing
Fragment names are document-**global** and unique
Every declared fragment must actually be used
A spread cycle is a validation error, not a hang
A fragment cannot declare variables — it borrows the op's

blocks.note: each fragment sits by its component

blocks.title: Colocation
blocks.text: A component declares the fragment for the data it renders, so the requirement travels with the component. One shared query can no longer drift from what components use.

blocks.note: with $full false, Stats' resolvers never run

blocks.title: Relay only
blocks.text: `@arguments` / `@argumentDefinitions` give fragments local variables — a client extension, not core spec.

blocks.title: One line to remember
blocks.text: On a union, select only `__typename` directly; every other field goes inside a fragment.

caption.text: Two fragments ask for the same field with different arguments, and the whole operation fails validation. Part 4 of GRAPHQL OPERATIONS covers grouping fields under one directive, fragment rules and colocation, unions vs interfaces, and how field merging decides what comes back.
